model_annotation: Figure 4 presents the number of participants who rated different aspects of a web-based tool as either high or low. The horizontal axis, labeled “Number of Participants,” displays a linear scale ranging from 0 to 6, with tick marks at each integer value. The vertical axis categorizes participant responses into five aspects: “Relevance #Cs”, “Summary”, “Clarity and Simplicity”, “Overall Quality”, and “Veracity Explanation”. Each aspect is represented by a pair of bars; a blue bar indicating the number of participants who rated the aspect as “high” and a grey bar indicating those who rated it as “low”. For “Relevance #Cs”, the "high" bar reaches approximately 5 participants while the "low" bar reaches 1. “Summary” has a "high" bar at about 4 participants and a "low" bar at approximately 2. “Clarity and Simplicity” has both "high" and "low" bars at about 3 participants. “Overall Quality” displays a "high" bar at approximately 2 participants and a "low" bar at about 4. The “Veracity Explanation” aspect shows the largest discrepancy, with a "high" bar at 1 participant and a "low" bar at 5. The bars are arranged alphabetically based on the aspect labels. No bars are visually emphasized through shading, bolding, outlines, or annotations.
